headline: Third AAP MLA resigns in two days as Kunwar Vijay Pratap quits
content: Chandigarh, Nov 2: In a major development in Punjab's ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Amritsar North MLA, Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, resigned on Monday, following in the footsteps of two other MLAs who resigned the previous day.Singh, a former IPS officer, also sent his resignation letter to the Punjab Assembly Speaker on Monday.He was suspended by the AAP for five years in June 2025 for alleged anti-party activities as he had opposed the arrest of Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) leader Bikram Singh Majithia in a Disproportionate Assets case.Sharing the information on X, Singh said that he will remain "indebted to you until my last breath for the love and respect you have shown me", referring to the people of the state."With your cooperation and the blessings of the Almighty, we must all unite in a collective effort to rise above the politics of lanes and ribbon-cutting, and transform Punjab—trapped by drugs, extortion, gangsterism, and corruption—back into a progressive and beloved state," he said.Singh asserted that he had achieved "90 per cent targets", adding that his "greatest achievement" is "ending the 'mai-baap' culture in politics and working by considering the public as my source of inspiration"."In the Punjab Legislative Assembly, I always raised the voice of Amritsaris and boldly addressed issues from water and sewage to Circuit House, Company Bagh, dirty drains, Guru Nanak Dev University, Government Medical College, Saroop Rani College, and the Bargari sacrilege case. This was the first time that area-specific issues were raised by me in the Punjab Legislative Assembly by naming lanes and neighbourhoods," he said."Working together with you to formulate a forward strategy, my aim will be to ensure clean politics and transparent administration. My sole purpose is 'Punjab First'. Apart from this, I will have no personal interests," he added.Earlier on Sunday, Singh had hit out at AAP National Convener Arvind Kejriwal and Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, asserting that the party had strayed from its founding ideals.Pratap's exit follows the resignations of fellow MLAs, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jouramajra, who resigned from the AAP's primary membership and the Assembly on Sunday.Pathanmajra, who represents the Sanour Assembly constituency in Patiala district, sent his resignation letter to Arvind Kejriwal, announcing his decision to quit the party with immediate effect.Pathanmajra has been at the centre of several controversies in the past. A rape case was registered against him, following which he travelled to Australia. He was subsequently arrested by the police after returning to India to join the investigation into the case.Meanwhile, Jouramajra, who represents the Samana Assembly constituency and has also served as a minister in the Punjab government, announced his resignation through a social media post.According to media reports, tensions had reportedly been building between him and the party leadership after the AAP high command appointed former senior Shiromani Akali Dal leader Surjit Singh Rakhra as the in-charge of the Samana Assembly constituency.The decision had reportedly left Jouramajra unhappy with the party leadership, as the appointment of another leader as constituency in-charge in his own Assembly seat was viewed as a setback to his political standing and influence in the area.The resignations come at a crucial time for the AAP, which is facing a political challenge ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. --IANS

headline: Fire truck bursts into flames following accident in Udaipur; 2 burnt to death
content: Two men were burnt to death, and two others sustained injuries after a fire tender collided with a trailer before hitting another vehicle and bursting into flames in Rajasthan’s Udaipur district, police said on Sunday.The accident occurred when the fire tender, belonging to a private firm, was travelling from Gujarat towards Udaipur.Rishabhdev Station House Officer Hemant Ahari said the vehicle first rammed into a trailer moving ahead of it and went out of control, before hitting a truck in another lane.The impact caused the fire tender’s cabin to catch fire, trapping three people inside.Locals managed to pull the driver out of the burning vehicle, but the two other occupants were burnt to death. Their identities are yet to be established, police said.The drivers of the fire tender and the trailer have sustained injuries and are undergoing treatment at MB Hospital in Udaipur.Police said efforts are under way to identify the deceased and contact the company that owned the fire truck.

headline: Tens of thousands protest against Narendra Modi regime in Delhi | India
content: Led by Congress party, India’s opposition alliance channels anger over removal of 130 million names from voter roll Thousands of opposition supporters have gathered in Delhi as protests against the Narendra Modi government continue to gather momentum. Led by the Congress party, India’s opposition alliance has brought together supporters from across the country, amid growing anger over a large-scale revision of the country’s voter roll that has seen 130 million names erased. Opposition leaders have alleged the process gives Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) an electoral advantage, and have called for the resignation and impeachment of the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar. The BJP has denied the claims. Addressing tens of thousands of party workers and supporters, the opposition leader Rahul Gandhi said Kumar had “carried out the biggest crime. He has tried to silence the voice of people, strangulate our country.” Gandhi said the opposition, united under the acronym India (Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance), would not let “democracy be finished in the country” and warned Modi: “You can’t run anywhere.”

headline: West Bengal government notifies jobs for kin of those killed in political violence
content: Kolkata The West Bengal government on Sunday (November 1, 2026) issued a notification providing jobs for family members of those killed in political violence, a day after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced the decision on Saturday (October 31, 2026) while addressing a gathering in Paschim Medinipur’s Garbeta. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/west-bengal/ “Apply to the DM (District Magistrate). We will give Group D jobs to you,” Mr. Adhikari had said, referring to the families that have been at the receiving end of political violence. The notification, signed by West Bengal Chief Secretary Manoj Agarwal on Sunday, stated that one member of the family of each person who had lost their life in political clashes would be provided employment by the State government. West Bengal CM promises CAA certificates to 2.5 lakh Matuas by end of 2026 West Bengal CM promises CAA certificates to 2.5 lakh Matuas by end of 2026 During his first visit to Thakurbari in North 24 Parganas after taking up the office of Chief Minister, Suvendu Adhikari says West Bengal would have turned into Bangladesh had the BJP not come to power in 2026 West Bengal CM promises CAA certificates to 2.5 lakh Matuas by end of 2026 storyline 1 The appointments will be made at the Group D level as a one-time exception, without affecting normal recruitment. The notification provides a cut-off date from 2001 onwards. Families with victims of political violence over the past 25 years can apply for government jobs. The 25 years marks the approximately 11 years during which the Left Front government was in power in the State, with the remaining years when the Trinamool Congress was in power. West Bengal has recorded several instances of political violence, particularly in the panchayat elections held in the State, over the past few decades. The BJP leadership has alleged that their supporters were targeted by Trinamool Congress after 2016, and that a large number of the party’s supporters were targeted after the 2021 Assembly election. The scheme has several eligibility criteria, which includes that the family’s monthly income should not be more than ₹50,000. The applicant will have to provide details of the incident, along with the FIR, death certificate and relationship with the deceased. A screening committee led by District Magistrates and Superintendents of Police will examine the applications. Eligible applicants will include the spouse, son, daughter or third-gender child of the deceased. In cases where an unmarried person was killed, a brother or sister may also be considered, subject to specified conditions. Only one member from each eligible family will be considered for appointment.
